text:
Thomas Chabot has 12 points in 20 games, a pace above the middle of his talent range and well above the typical defenseman. Ottawa has carried play with him out there: 57.6% of the 5v5 expected goals, the quality of chances, a strong number for anyone logging 23:24 a night.

The odd part is the trend. Over his last ten he has eight points, all but one of them assists, yet his ice time is down more than three minutes a night from what he's used to. Some of the shine is luck too: Ottawa has scored about five more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, so the assist pile may slow.

Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among 215 defensemen last season, almost all of it from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a defensive wrinkle: he stopped 16% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman. After the 6-5 overtime loss to Philadelphia, TSN's headline had him saying “We have to turn the page and focus on Saturday”. Ottawa beat the Kings that Saturday.
headline: Chabot's points are back, his minutes are down
